title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
summary: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math Release.

title: Phases in the cyclic quantum dilogarithm: correction to "Cyclic quantum Teichmüller theory"
summary: We first correct $\boldsymbolμ_N$-phase issues in the basic definition around the cyclic quantum dilogarithm operators in [Ish26]. In particular, the notion of global coefficients must be extended by incorporating additional lifting data forming a $\boldsymbolμ_N$-cover, and the pentagon relation generally acquires an extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor is trivial. Consequently, the original statements of [Ish26] hold for such lifts and are therefore restored.

title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
comment: Preliminary draft version, 24 pages. Comments are welcome!
summary: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $θ_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $θ_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel. Central elements act by the outer automorphisms of the simple currents. In types A, D, E the level-one class is computed by comparing maximal-torus jump loops with the lattice $α$-induction construction of the companion paper on both current and charged generators, followed by integral degree-four Cartan restriction. Higher levels follow by tensor additivity, and the remaining types by restriction along index-one embeddings into simply laced groups. As a consequence, for every compact simply connected semisimple $G$, every class in $H^4(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ is the obstruction of a $G$-kernel on the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor.

title: On the complexification of $ q $-deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups
summary: For the quantised algebra of functions on a simply connected compact semisimple Lie group, we study the relationship between the primitive spectrum, topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on Hilbert spaces, and quantum holomorphic evaluations induced via the Drinfeld double. In terms of the Joseph stratification of the primitive spectrum, we prove a sharp dichotomy: primitive ideals in homogeneous strata always arise as kernels of topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on a Hilbert space, whereas those in inhomogeneous strata do not admit any such realisations. We further show that, unlike in the classical situation, quantum holomorphic evaluations typically fail to be topologically irreducible, and that their kernels do not determine the primitive spectrum. Finally, we describe the Iwasawa decomposition of the Drinfeld double in terms of polynomial functions, extending work by Podleś-Woronowicz for the quantum Lorentz group to all complex semisimple quantum groups, and clarifying the structure of quantum holomorphic evaluations.

title: Typical representations of admissible type I algebraic supergroups
summary: We study typical representations of an admissible type I algebraic supergroup $G$. We prove that, for a dominant weight $λ$, the induced supermodule $H^0_G(λ)$ is simple if and only if $λ$ is typical and the induced module $H^0_{G_{\mathrm{ev}}}(λ)$ for the even subgroup $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is simple. We establish equivalences between typical blocks for $G$ and blocks for $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$, and give a projectivity criterion for Kac modules over every Frobenius kernel. For connected $SpO(2\ell|2)$ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, we classify all simple projective supermodules over Frobenius kernels.

title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
summary: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.

title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
comment: The proof is simplified and shortened further relative to the previous version. A discussion about the Lie brackets and the generators is added
summary: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.
